findings: The source unambiguously defines beautiful numbers by one to three zero bits excluding leading zeros, inclusive query endpoints, and modulus 998244353.
The source supplies full bounds Q <= 200000 and 1 <= L <= R <= 10^18.
The published example and explanation are both incorrect. In [5,8], valid numbers are 5,6,8 with cube sum 853. In [10,15], valid numbers are 10,11,12,13,14 with cube sum 9000.
A recovery must disclose these corrections instead of preserving the incorrect [153,0] or the incomplete explanation's 637.

An original implementation can enumerate at most three cleared nonleading bits for each bit length, sort eligible numbers and build modular cube prefix sums, then answer each query by binary search. Full-domain runtime and memory still require sandbox measurement.
